old_problem: The row's explicit fields span two standard structures: Type 18 memory-error metadata and Type 3 chassis identity/status/security. The prior review preserved the conflict but requested a new owner mapping; DeepSeek's header-only Type 18 grep would test neither full Type 18 payload nor any Type 3 field.
disposition_reason: Resolve Pending and Source Conflict using the DMTF SMBIOS field definitions. Type 18 owns Error Type, Granularity, Operation, Vendor Syndrome, Memory Array/Device Error Address and Error Resolution. Type 3 owns Manufacturer, chassis Type, Version, Serial, Asset Tag, Boot-up, Power Supply, Thermal and Security Status. Both branches are mandatory because both appear in the Procedure; neither substitutes for the other. Exact expected matrices and reboot parameters are fail-closed Project Configuration. Logs remain preserved.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1935, same-row tests.json/DeepSeek, GPT V2, historical record, shared-code row 1933 and ED-01 through ED-30 were read. The actual next formal row was directly opened as Functionality 1936 / Wistron-BIOS-00478-V002 / 7c13341839f66e11.

DMTF SMBIOS defines every listed memory-error field in Type 18 and the listed chassis identity/status/security fields in Type 3, so field ownership is technically determinable without deleting copied-looking coverage.
Row 1933's Type 12 variant stays independent despite the shared code. This row validates Type 18 plus its explicit Type 3 companion branch only.
Complete structures, handles, all payload fields, stdout/stderr/status and semantic comparisons are required; a heading grep cannot pass.
One approved warm reboot uses same-target Boot ID and OS Ready proof. Log clearing is rejected because it destroys the pre/post evidence window.
No dmidecode, SSH, reboot, log-clear, firmware, SMBIOS, security or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_name: SMBIOS Type 18 memory-error plus Type 3 chassis-field correctness and reboot persistence
test_case.purpose: Validate every Type 18 32-Bit Memory Error Information field and every explicitly listed Type 3 chassis identity/status/security field against versioned Project matrices before and after one approved warm reboot.
required_package: Exact SUT/board/BIOS/SMBIOS identity and versioned Type 18 error-field plus Type 3 chassis-field expected matrices
Validated dmidecode and complete Type 18/Type 3 parsers preserving handles, multiplicity, raw output, stderr/status and sensitive-field redaction
Secure authenticated host access and protected evidence storage
Approved OS warm reboot, workload window, Boot ID/OS Ready timeout and independent console/BMC recovery
Preserved dmesg/syslog/SEL baseline and explicit separation from same-code Type 12 row
test_case.test_command: READ-ONLY COLLECTION AROUND ONE APPROVED REBOOT; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind target/BIOS/SMBIOS identity and preserve logs. Run authenticated privileged `dmidecode --type 18` and `dmidecode --type 3` without grep or error suppression; save complete raw output/status. Parse all Type 18 error fields and all listed Type 3 identity/status fields against their separate approved matrices. After point-of-action approval, perform one OS warm reboot, prove same-target Boot ID change and OS Ready, then repeat both complete collections and semantic diffs. Do not clear logs, expose credentials, merge Type 12, modify firmware/SMBIOS/security or automatically retry.
test_case.expected_result: Every expected Type 18 structure has correct Error Type, Granularity, Operation, Vendor Syndrome, array/device addresses and Resolution; the Type 3 structure has correct Manufacturer, chassis Type, Version, Serial, Asset Tag and four status/security values. Both complete sets remain semantically correct and stable after the same target reaches OS Ready, with no unexplained health regression.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact identity, successful complete pre/post Type 18 and Type 3 collection, every expected field/multiplicity correct, approved Boot ID-changing warm reboot and OS Ready. FAIL on missing/extra/malformed structures, field mismatch, bad address/handle semantics, unexpected persistence change, command/reboot/health failure or incomplete evidence. NOT READY covers absent matrices/access/reboot/recovery. A header grep, Type 18-only or Type 3-only output cannot PASS; end user owns verdict.
safety_gate: Collection is read-only; never change BIOS, SMBIOS, chassis security, firmware or recipe state.
Preserve complete logs/raw output and protect addresses, serials, asset tags and security metadata; never clear or suppress errors.
Use secure verified access; never expose passwords or disable host verification.
Require explicit reboot/workload approval and independent recovery; do not automatically retry or substitute cold/DC/AC cycling.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant and separate Type 12 variant, target/BIOS/SMBIOS/dmidecode/parser identity and both expected matrices
Complete pre/post Type 18 raw/parsed error records with handles and all listed fields
Complete pre/post Type 3 raw/parsed chassis identity/status/security records with protected values
Approved reboot timeline, Boot IDs, same-target OS Ready and preserved platform logs/health
No-clear/no-write/no-merge/no-retry audit, evidence hashes, workload restore and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On reboot failure, retain first evidence and use only the approved console/BMC boot-recovery runbook; do not reboot again automatically. On missing, malformed or changed Type 18/Type 3 data, preserve full SMBIOS tables and firmware identity, make no BIOS/SMBIOS/security edit and escalate to the BIOS/platform owner. Do not use the Type 12 row to replace either branch.
